results.name: mac-move
results.title: MAC move between MLAG peers and back
results.action: Switches the MAC-move host's active-backup bond from its link to CHR 1 to its link to CHR 2, keeping the same MAC and IP address, then switches it back after 4 s.

phases.name: Move to CHR 2
phases.expected: The host's gratuitous ARP enters CHR 2 on ether5, a regular bridge port without mlag-id. CHR 2 moves the host MAC to ether5 in its bridge host table and floods the broadcast to its local ports and over the peer port; CHR 1 floods it only to its regular port ether5 and moves the MAC to the peer port ether2. Lab target: no probe to or from the host is lost, and once the gratuitous ARP reaches CHR 2, no frame addressed to the host MAC leaves CHR 1 on ether5.

phases.name: Move back to CHR 1
phases.expected: The host's gratuitous ARP enters CHR 1 on ether5. CHR 1 moves the host MAC back to ether5 and floods the broadcast to its local ports and over the peer port; CHR 2 floods it only to its regular port ether5 and moves the MAC to the peer port ether2. Lab target: no probe to or from the host is lost, and from the moment the gratuitous ARP reaches CHR 1 to the end of the recovery window, no frame addressed to the host MAC leaves CHR 2 on ether5.

results.name: member-flap-repeat
results.title: Repeated MLAG bond member flap
results.action: Takes client 1's bond member to CHR 1 (ether3) down at both ends for 1 s and back up for 3 s, five times, then watches 8 s of return plus a 3 s recovery window. Both MLAG peers' bridge host table entries for client 2 and the MAC-move host are sampled every 0.35 s throughout.

phases.name: Five member flaps
phases.expected: Each flap removes ether3 from CHR 1's MLAG bond client1 and adds it back once LACP renegotiates. While the member is down, CHR 1 forwards traffic for client 1 over the peer link to CHR 2, with brief loss. This phase runs from the first flap to the fifth return, so it holds four complete flaps and the fifth down; result.json lists the loss of every flap separately. Each loss of streams 101, 201 and 302 may last at most 3 s, the member limit per flap. Streams 102 and 202 never touch client 1 and lose nothing, and the bridge host table entries for client 2 and the MAC-move host stay on both MLAG peers. The field report saw unrelated MACs move to the peer port after a member flap.
failed_checks: 501 broadcast from client 1: no second sighting at the sender's bond members during withdrawal, seq [120]
502 unknown unicast from client 1: no second sighting at the sender's bond members during withdrawal, seq [120, 204]

phases.name: Member back after the fifth flap
phases.expected: Carrier returns for the last time and LACP renegotiates ether3 with client 1 until it shows synchronization, collecting and distributing (S, C, D). Loss of streams 101, 201 and 302 lasts at most 3 s. Streams 102 and 202 and both bypass streams lose nothing, and the host entries for client 2 and the MAC-move host stay present.

results.action: Switches the MAC-move host's active-backup bond from its link to CHR 1 to its link to CHR 2, keeping the same MAC and IP address, then switches it back after 4 s.

phases.name: Move to CHR 2
phases.expected: The host's gratuitous ARP enters CHR 2 on ether5, a regular bridge port without mlag-id. CHR 2 moves the host MAC to ether5 in its bridge host table and floods the broadcast to its local ports and over the peer port; CHR 1 floods it only to its regular port ether5 and moves the MAC to the peer port ether2. Lab target: no probe to or from the host is lost, and once the gratuitous ARP reaches CHR 2, no frame addressed to the host MAC leaves CHR 1 on ether5.

phases.name: Move back to CHR 1
phases.expected: The host's gratuitous ARP enters CHR 1 on ether5. CHR 1 moves the host MAC back to ether5 and floods the broadcast to its local ports and over the peer port; CHR 2 floods it only to its regular port ether5 and moves the MAC to the peer port ether2. Lab target: no probe to or from the host is lost, and from the moment the gratuitous ARP reaches CHR 1 to the end of the recovery window, no frame addressed to the host MAC leaves CHR 2 on ether5.

results.name: member-flap-repeat
results.title: Repeated MLAG bond member flap
results.action: Takes client 1's bond member to CHR 1 (ether3) down at both ends for 1 s and back up for 3 s, five times, then watches 8 s of return plus a 3 s recovery window. Both MLAG peers' bridge host table entries for client 2 and the MAC-move host are sampled every 0.35 s throughout.

phases.name: Five member flaps
phases.expected: Each flap removes ether3 from CHR 1's MLAG bond client1 and adds it back once LACP renegotiates. While the member is down, CHR 1 forwards traffic for client 1 over the peer link to CHR 2, with brief loss. This phase runs from the first flap to the fifth return, so it holds four complete flaps and the fifth down; result.json lists the loss of every flap separately. Each loss of streams 101, 201 and 302 may last at most 3 s, the member limit per flap. Streams 102 and 202 never touch client 1 and lose nothing, and the bridge host table entries for client 2 and the MAC-move host stay on both MLAG peers. The field report saw unrelated MACs move to the peer port after a member flap.
failed_checks: 502 unknown unicast from client 1: no second sighting at the sender's bond members during withdrawal, seq [196]

phases.name: Member back after the fifth flap
phases.expected: Carrier returns for the last time and LACP renegotiates ether3 with client 1 until it shows synchronization, collecting and distributing (S, C, D). Loss of streams 101, 201 and 302 lasts at most 3 s. Streams 102 and 202 and both bypass streams lose nothing, and the host entries for client 2 and the MAC-move host stay present.
failed_checks: 501 broadcast from client 1: no second sighting at the sender's bond members during restoration, seq [236]

results.name: peer-link-loss
results.title: Peer link loss and return
results.action: Cuts the peer link (ether2) at both MLAG peers, holds it down for 15 s, restores it and watches 65 s of return.

phases.name: Peer link down
phases.expected: Both MLAG peers lose ICCP and leave mlag-state connected. With mlag-lacp-fallback=yes the MLAG secondary stops using the shared system ID, so the clients renegotiate LACP and keep their member to the primary, with brief loss.

phases.name: Peer link back
phases.expected: ICCP returns to mlag-state connected on both peers and the secondary takes the shared system ID again. The clients renegotiate LACP with brief loss.
